questions.problem:
Determine the area $A$ of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

$\,\,A=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-2)-5\cdot 7 \\  & =2-35 \\  & =-33\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,-33\,|=33
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Parallelogram Spanned by Two Parallel Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & a \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & a \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2\sqrt{2})\cdot 6-a\cdot 3 \\  & =12\sqrt{2}-3a\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12\sqrt{2}-3a & =0 \\ -3a & =-12\sqrt{2} \\ a & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}-2\cdot 1 \\  & =2-2 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\textbf{u}=\langle 1,2 \rangle$ and $\textbf{v}=\langle 3, -3 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-3)-3\cdot 2 \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $\det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A = |{-9}| = 9
$$
